solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sauce boat at a higher price

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
prices that have gone up are higher

explanation.surface: A gravy boat that costs more than it used to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as one item, a gravy boat; split it so 'Sauce' is the definition and 'boat' is a ketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato-based table condiment, the commonest bottled sauce.

clue.text: Abduction of a kind, getting mixed press initially

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters are jumbled together
initially takes the first letter of the word press

explanation.surface: A sort of abduction, reported in a confused way by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges A KIND into KIDNA, then P is added from 'press initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing and carrying off a person by force, usually for ransom.

clue.text: Score individual required in game

parts.note: a score is twenty
an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: A player needs to score in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon or blackjack, the card game where you aim for this total.

clue.text: Speed shown in running heats

indicators.note: running signals the letters of heats move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Speed on display in the heats of a running race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' suits the athletics picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry or swiftness of movement, a synonym of rapidity.

clue.text: Say it, perhaps this, to a Parisian

parts.note: it is an example of a pronoun, shown by perhaps
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A French speaker being told to say a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter or articulate a word, or to declare formally.

clue.text: Heading for Rotterdam, old vessel carrying English fruit

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the word Rotterdam is taken
the vessel word holds the English abbreviation inside it, as a ship carries cargo

parts.note: a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: An old ship heads for Rotterdam with English fruit aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed-pod of a wild rose bush is a fruit, used for syrup and tea.

clue.text: Automated machine, British in origin

indicators.note: in places the British abbreviation inside the word for source

parts.note: a root is an origin or source

explanation.surface: A machine that was invented in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British in origin' reads as made in Britain, but it means B goes inside ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical device that carries out tasks by itself, without a human operator.

clue.text: Tommy planned to keep going

parts.note: Tommy, short for Tommy Atkins, is slang for a British private soldier
something on is scheduled or planned, as in the party is on

explanation.surface: A British infantryman meant to carry on fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British army private, from the name Tommy Atkins.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to persevere doggedly in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: The man and daughter, catching on, pointed

indicators.note: catching means the pronoun grabs the next word inside itself

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A father and daughter cottoning on to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching on' reads as understanding, but 'catching' is the containment signal acting on the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpened, as a blade ground to an edge or a point.

clue.text: Excuse certain to cause amusement

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A confident excuse that is bound to amuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment or delight, as in reading for fun.

clue.text: Prepare to get into gear

definitions.meaning: to prepare food, as in ... a chicken or a salad
to put on clothes, gear being slang for clothing

explanation.surface: Getting ready to start moving, like a car going into gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing a salad readies it; dressing yourself puts on your clothing, or gear.

clue.text: All things considered, loan can be arranged

indicators.note: arranged signals the preceding letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Weighing everything up, a bank loan can be set up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning taking everything into account, weighing the pros and cons.

clue.text: Not more than that new, imperfect tomes

indicators.note: new signals that the word that is remade into a fresh order
imperfect signals the word tomes is spoiled into a rearranged order

explanation.surface: Something no better than those new but flawed books.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'new' rearranges THAT into ATTH and 'imperfect' rearranges TOMES into EMOST.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom setting an upper limit, meaning no greater than a given amount.

clue.text: Religious people spending hour in river

indicators.note: spending means giving up, so the hour abbreviation is used up and gone

parts.note: Hindus are followers of the Hindu religion

explanation.surface: Pilgrims passing an hour in a sacred river.
explanation.definitionFit: A major river of Pakistan, flowing from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Dog in a grand bordello, barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog barking in a grand brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise, but it is British slang for crazy and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular retriever breed with a yellow coat, used as a guide animal.

clue.text: Sinister drug, an unknown quantity

parts.note: dark can mean sinister or evil
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A sinister drug whose effects nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a competitor whose abilities are little known but who may surprise.

clue.text: Bird in brass — a lot manufactured

indicators.note: manufactured signals the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A brass bird made in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A large seabird with a huge wingspan, of the southern oceans.

clue.text: Timber washed ashore did for odd couple inside

indicators.note: inside places the number word within the rearranged letters
odd means strange, so the letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: Wood on the beach that finished off a strange pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges DID FOR into DRIFOD, and 'inside' puts TWO within it: DRIF-TWO-OD. 'odd couple' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood that has floated on the sea and been cast up on a beach.

clue.text: Takes in better paper

parts.note: to take someone in is to fool them
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Someone who absorbs better quality paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional large size of writing or printing sheet.

clue.text: Be on it, and dream wildly?

definitions.text: Be on it, and dream wildly?

indicators.note: wildly signals the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Bet on the fruit machine and fantasise about a jackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: someone gambling on a slot machine dreams wildly of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a slot or fruit machine, named for its lever arm and for robbing players.

clue.text: Lace nutty Irish cake

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go mad into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irish cake decorated with lace and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutty' sounds like a cake ingredient but signals the anagram of LACE, giving ECLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Check on tailless bird in tree

indicators.note: tailless means the bird word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lark is a songbird
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Looking at a bird without a tail sitting in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-or-across charade 'on' can mean placed after; here the chess abbreviation follows the docked bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer with needles that fall each autumn.

clue.text: Compass showing north in storm

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the word for fury

parts.note: to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A compass pointing north during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' is not the instrument but scope or extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent, as in the full span of something.

clue.text: Flag-waving threesome in pact I suspect

indicators.note: in places the group of three inside the rearranged letters
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are unreliable and reordered

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A dubious pact between three nationalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges PACT I into PATIC, and 'in' puts TRIO inside it: PA-TRIO-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving a national flag is a show of love for one's country.

clue.text: Guide the Italian aboard vessel

indicators.note: aboard places the article inside the container word

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian helping steer a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container: a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to steer or lead a course, as a harbour navigator does.

clue.text: Crazy firing head of security — senseless

indicators.note: firing means dismissing, so a letter is sacked from the word

parts.note: insane means crazy

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word security is taken

explanation.surface: A mad decision to sack the head of security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' removes S, the head of 'security', from INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or lacking sense, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Rule mostly broken by key singer

indicators.note: broken by means the shortened word is split open to take the key inside
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: to control is to rule
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A rule broken by a singer hitting a key note.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is the computer keyboard key, not a musical one, despite the singer in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female voice type, and a woman who sings in it.

clue.text: Member holding head of orchid with a distinctive smell

indicators.note: the limb word holds the flower's first letter inside it

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word orchid is taken

explanation.surface: Someone holding an orchid that has a distinctive scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant, characteristic scent, as of coffee or baking bread.

clue.text: Current offering

definitions.meaning: happening now, existing at this time

explanation.surface: An offering that is up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the adjective meaning happening now and the noun meaning a gift share this spelling.

clue.text: Narrow lake shown in poster

indicators.note: shown in puts the lake abbreviation inside the word for one who posts

parts.note: a poster is one who posts a letter, a sender
L is the standard abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A thin lake pictured on a wall poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' looks like a printed picture, but it is someone who posts things: a sender.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim or thin in width; a slight margin is also called this.
